title: Change Log
summary: Dated releases, smaller improvements and fixes.
body:
October30: faction standings — live testing

#factions now opens your faction standings with white text, numbers and full-range bars. Search by name, page through results or inspect your standing with a targeted NPC faction. No client update is needed; readability and gameplay acceptance remain in testing. Commands and limits.

October 30 — public Classic Cazic-Thule restored

Restored 188 Classic encounter points in open-world Cazic-Thule, which previously had no eligible combat population under Classic. Khaleid’s route now leads to the restored public encounters. Existing private Raid and Grind runs retain their own population and rewards. No client update is required; gameplay acceptance remains open.

Hate’s saved Raid population was also checked: every expected point was accounted for by living mobs, recorded kills or the final-boss gate. No Hate mobs were added. New-layout Grind and client visibility remain separate checks.

October 30: Commonlands recall labels corrected

Recall labels corrected (October 30): Client release 2026103001 restores Ancient Attunement’s name, Nightcap Recall’s hotbutton label and the recall description. Fully exit EverQuest and press Play in the normal launcher to update. Cast time, reuse and bind behavior are unchanged. In-game verification remains open.

October28: Bazaar posting and readable controls — live testing

Client update2026102803 accepts valid whole-platinum digits in both native text formats, reports unreadable input, and enlarges seller text with light colors. The earlier startup fixes and weapon changes are preserved. The owner confirmed the reported posting issue is resolved, the preview appears and the larger light text is readable. Broader market QA remains separate.

October 26: Bazaar seller panel and Paladin grips — live testing

Sell / My Listings controls

Client update 2026102601 adds the native Sell / My Listings tab for posting, cancelling owned listings and collecting offline proceeds. The paired server release also includes Paladin weapon grips. Close EverQuest and use launcher Play to update. Native gameplay acceptance remains open. Panel instructions.

October 26: Commonlands player bazaar — live testing

Persistent player listings, offline seller proceeds and native search/purchase routing are installed in public East Commonlands. No parked auctioneer is required. Native RoF2 search, buying and full seller/buyer acceptance remain open. Market instructions and restrictions.

October 24 — High Keep rescue, Ashen Compact and aggro corrections

New High Keep Raid runs now rescue Osargen. The level-50 Ashen Compact begins with Drazhul and the Keeper in the hidden Everfrost passage before Permafrost. Close EQ and use launcher Play for its helmet appearance. NPC departure cleanup and stationary return-home restoration are corrected; the original Lower Guk bedroom-train report still needs an observed retest. Existing earned progress is retained. Full route, escort, appearance and balance acceptance remain open.

October 24 — Ashen Compact entrance preview

Before the coordinated release above, the Shadow Knight campaign entrance was moved to the hidden Everfrost passage before Permafrost. Its frostbound crossing and return connect to curated Kael. At that preview stage it was a test candidate; the release above supersedes that availability.

October 24 - Multiclass tome learning repaired

Eligible tomes can now be learned through any held class, fixing secondary and third-class Rogue learning. Failed right-clicks preserve the original tome; full lists, duplicate entries and failed saves no longer consume it. Discipline use levels and the level-1 AA policy are unchanged. See learning combat disciplines for requirements. Live gameplay acceptance remains under review.

October 24 — Custom content on Features

Features now groups Raid & Grind dungeons, helmet quests, Zone Hunt, epic reforging, class armor, crafting, exploration and custom character systems. Each entry links to its guide. The Ashen Compact preview is explicitly not released; gameplay, rewards and balance are unchanged.

Current instructions live in Guides. This is the history of releases, improvements and fixes; older entries describe their date and may be superseded.

October 24, 2026 · A clearer wiki

Features now highlights the major differences from standard EQ. Guides start with useful instructions; fixes and repeated release announcements are collected here. Navigation and text sizes are consistent, and long reference lists expand when needed. Existing tools, gameplay rules, reward values and links are preserved.

October 24 · The Hole entrance

Live testing — keyless Hole entrance: The Hole Key and lock-picking requirement have been removed from the entrance rock in Paineel at /loc 568,-896,-96. Click the rock to open the passage without a key or lock picks. The server update is installed; in-game acceptance is pending. Paineel city-lift keys and the Sacred Key doors inside The Hole remain unchanged.

October 23: two AA per level and level-1 AA controls

The paired update is installed for live testing. Keep AA allocation at 0% to earn full leveling XP plus two AA per level. Use the AA +/− controls from level 1, choose an intermediate percentage, or select 100% to hold your level and grind AA. Full focus earns 20 AA per current-level equivalent of XP. Update through launcher Play for game 2026102301. Saved points, purchases and partial progress are retained; native gameplay acceptance remains open.

October 23 · The Vigil of the Dawn — live testing

October 23: Camil’s Chapterhouse quest, level-50–53 encounters, custom rewards, Ember augment, waypoint and Keeper are deployed for live testing. Native Tasks track the story. Full encounter balance and player acceptance remain open. Read the quest guide and reward catalog.

October 22: production loot finder

The class and era loot finder supports any held class by default, optional all-class matching, slot/quality/level/zone filters and item links to source mobs, locations and calculated drop chances. Production content refreshes automatically every fifteen minutes, with the last successful capture retained if a refresh fails. Existing gameplay, rewards and acceptance labels are unchanged.

Live testing — Hate Keeper in Commonlands: Find the Plane of Hate Keeper in East Commonlands at /loc -1570,-346,3, between Mirielle and Khalure in the travel area. Raid, Grind and return entry lead to Hate; private Hate instances retain an entrance Keeper. Public and private Hate entry require level 46; GM status is no longer required. The server update is installed. The owner confirmed the relocation, Commonlands visibility and Hate travel. Broader dungeon balance and full-clear QA remain separate.

Build Lab — October 22

The experimental Build Lab compares two saved builds, supported spell benefits, Hunt item stat differences and editable ability priorities. Inspect mana and cast timelines or search the best priority order under your test conditions. It uses dated source controls and explicit assumptions, not a complete native combat simulation or universal best-build ranking.

October 22 — Your interactive field guide

The wiki has a new lantern-lit design with four adventure paths, instant quick search, saved guides, light and dark reading modes, and a reading-progress bar. The equipment catalog keeps its filters and all four reward qualities. On the home page, expand Release notes & live testing for the existing gameplay notices. Learn the shortcuts and field notes →

Live testing: The Classic raid rewards give every dungeon three exclusive designs. The 14 added dungeons contribute 42 designs in two qualities; all 414 dungeon rewards are MAGIC. Fear, Hate and Sky receive lore-driven relics and equipped utility clicks. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

October 22 — every Classic dungeon and unique rewards live

Live testing: Every Classic dungeon coverage adds the same Raid/Grind choices in 21 combat dungeon zones, including Fear, Hate and Sky. All 21 are installed for live testing; gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

The paired release also repairs stale dungeon item checks behind the reported Keeper error and installs durable Sky key services. Existing runs, earned rewards and the latest quest-tier and client updates are preserved. Native gameplay and balance acceptance remain open.

October 22 - quest ingredient fix live for testing

Polished, Exalted and Ascended ingredients can satisfy Normal quest requirements, including Aviak Charm for Crafted Gauntlets. Shared hand-ins, task delivery and five older Temple quests are covered. The paired server and quest release is deployed; player QA remains open. Scope and limits.

October 22 — Ascended class-armor quest rewards

Crafted, Lambent, Darkforge, Ivy Etched and Totemic quests now grant 37 reviewed Ascended armor rewards. Substantial repeatable class-armor quests qualify; cheap/basic hand-ins remain excluded. The dependent Darkforge epic turn-in accepts Normal and Ascended pieces. Existing owned gear is not automatically converted. Live testing: native delivery and balance acceptance remain open. Scope and testing.

October 22 · Waypoint crystals — live testing

Waypoints now have a glowing crystal with the existing a waypoint label. Fully close EverQuest, then use the normal launcher’s Play button to install game 2026102202 before testing. The crystal adds a model to the portal effect; appearance in Classic and Modern model modes and with particles low or off still needs in-game checks. Locations, discovery progress and return destinations are unchanged.

October 22 — robe waist correction in live testing

Game update 2026102204 repairs the native waist binding after the earlier 2026102203 repair failed, covering all seven added Classic robe races and both genders. Close the game, reopen the normal launcher and press Play. In-game visual, dye and animation acceptance remains open. Read the scope.

October 22 — Dungeon Keeper placement

The correction now separates Keepers from overlapping waypoints in Befallen, Unrest, Najena, Permafrost and Nagafen’s Lair. High Keep and Cazic-Thule already had separate positions. All seven Keeper locations are listed for live testing; visibility remains unconfirmed. Waypoints, dungeon progress and client files are unchanged.

Level-scaled AA — live testing: Earn two AA per level while leveling. From level 1, use the AA +/− buttons to choose 0–100%; 100% pauses leveling so you can grind AA where you prefer. Close EverQuest and update through launcher Play for game 2026102301. Existing points, purchases and partial progress stay intact. AA progression and examples.

October 21: slower AA earning and XP boost retirement

The October 21 release used 1,000,000 AA experience per point with 10% passive earning; the October 23 level-scaled update supersedes that earning model. Goldwind’s paid package is retired, Matron’s free buffs remain, and XP boost durations are respected. Existing points and purchases remain intact. Live balance testing continues.

October 19 · THJ behavior and stock gear — live testing

The custom AA, spell focus and stock-derived gear update is installed for live testing. Scaling uses 131 researched Legendary items and matching standard EverQuest baselines. Classic level 50 and starter progression are preserved. Reopen the normal launcher for game 2026101902 before testing. See behavior details and open testing limits.

October 19: all-class AA update

Live AA testing: All 16 classes have more earned AA options: 75 newly available lines, 111 expanded lines and Druid access to Healing Boon. No existing line is removed. Classic remains level 50. Reconnect and turn Recommended AA off to browse your held classes. Read the AA update.

Launch repair published: Game update 2026101901 corrects the client catalog mismatch that blocked Play after the previous update. Close EverQuest and the launcher, reopen your normal Nightcap shortcut, and press Play to receive the repair. Your game settings and the other managed files are preserved. Native login and gameplay confirmation remain open.

October 18: item, spell, pet and melee release

Live testing: Selected Ascended items now use reviewed THJ values. Direct damage adds effective Spell Damage, ordinary DoT ticks add half, and heroic INT/WIS improve direct values. Starter quality steps remain modest below comparable Normal dungeon equipment.

The same release adds paged permanent-pet equipment, bounded owner-stat inheritance, earned pet/melee AA updates, separate Rabid Bear benefit and illusion effects, and shared 750 base caps with Hunt headroom. Close EverQuest and use the launcher for game update 2026101802. Classic level 50 remains active; gameplay and balance acceptance are still open.

October 18 - More ordinary quality loot

Polished, Exalted and Ascended now have 20%, 5% and 1% chances per eligible ordinary equipment/bag drop. Hunt, dungeon and quest rewards are unchanged. Already generated loot is not rerolled.

October 18, 2026: built-in item colors

The Reforging Box and zone forging now accept an item's built-in color. This fixes ordinary items such as Dagger of Marnek being rejected as customized. A different player-applied dye color and the other customization restrictions still prevent combining. Recipes remain three Normal/Base copies or four higher-quality copies. No client update is required for this fix; in-game acceptance remains open.

October 18, 2026: separate ability cooldowns

Activated AA families now have independent cooldowns, including Rampage and Purify Body. Item and discipline timer collisions are also repaired. Existing saved waits keep their original expiry. Reconnect and test your abilities; generic skill and content-defined groups remain under review.

October 18, 2026: Classic travel file repair

Signed game update 2026101801 adds automatic missing/corrupt terrain and object archive repair for 17 Classic travel destinations, including West Commonlands, Misty Thicket and Toxxulia. Close EverQuest and press Play in the usual launcher. Existing gameplay assets and player settings are preserved; native zoning acceptance remains open.

October 17, 2026: progression, combat and crafting
  • The optional Recommended AA filter provides an early survival, sustain and damage shortlist across held classes.
  • Passive AA is now 10%, preserving full leveling EXP, earned points and 4,000 AA XP per point.
  • Six basic Monk attacks have separate reuse. Cooldown duration repairs address excessive and restarted timers; other shared identities remain under investigation.
  • Normal death costs no EXP or levels; prior losses are not refunded.
  • Stackable items support at least 100, retaining larger limits.
  • The Reforging Box accepts three identical eligible Normal/Base copies for Polished. Higher recipes still cost four.
  • Idle zones can unload without ending their workers and triggering a whole-game restart.
  • Update through launcher Play for the matched client. Gameplay and balance acceptance continue.
October 16, 2026
  • The dungeon guide now lists every required boss and explains boss-stage notices, full-clear credit and Keeper Status when task objectives are blank.
  • Raid and Grind dungeons are deployed for live testing with personal boss checklists, shared rewards and exclusive Raid drops. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain open.
  • Features now gathers the major departures from Classic.
  • Equipment eligibility recognizes held classes and permits playable races when the class matches; remaining restrictions still apply.
  • Temporary AA buffs retain their timers; ordinary blessings remain lasting.
  • Mira Coinwell provides tunnel banking. Haldra stocks Leather Padding.
  • The wiki’s guides, commands and generated reward pages have been reviewed together against current release evidence.
October 13, 2026
  • Passive AA changed from 40% to 20%, preserving full normal XP and 4,000 AA XP per point.
  • All allowed AA ranks open at level 1; points, eligibility and prerequisite ranks remain.
  • Stacked tradeskill ingredients and Craft All are deployed.
  • The tunnel workshop layout is more spacious; the Unrest waypoint moved beside its entrance Keeper.
  • Supported divine summoned-hammer families have zero resale value.
  • The reported multiclass training/offhand issue and merchant Sell All button issue were confirmed resolved.
October 11–12, 2026
  • Reusable four-copy upgrades are available from Artisan Veyra; higher #zoneforge steps now use four copies.
  • LORE restrictions are disabled. Food and drink requirements were removed.
  • Early scribing allows eligible scrolls into the spellbook before their casting level.
  • Sell All protects food, drink, reagents and casting focus items.
  • The launcher uses personal access codes and shows patch summaries.
  • Waypoint portals and floating-eye Instance Keepers received visual corrections. The reported pet-summon crash was confirmed resolved.
October 9, 2026
  • 48 Classic reward zones, 384 reward variants, type-22 augments and zone forging launched.
  • Passive AA increased to 40% at that time; the October 13 reduction above supersedes that rate.
  • Always Loot / Never Loot controls, effective Spell Damage on Throw Stone, and retained spell gems after normal death were added.

Release labels describe availability, not completed balance or gameplay acceptance. See In development for candidates.

Earlier release detail

Notices previously repeated across guides are retained below for their original context. Use the current guides for today’s instructions.

Ascension quest: earlier update details

THJ behavior and stock gear — live testing

The custom AA, spell focus and stock-derived gear update is installed for live testing. Scaling uses 131 researched Legendary items and matching standard EverQuest baselines. Classic level 50 and starter progression are preserved. Reopen the normal launcher for game 2026101902 before testing. See behavior details and open testing limits.

Combat, buffs & recovery: earlier update details

Try the experimental Build Lab to compare stat changes and test spell priorities against explicit combat assumptions. Full gear, AA and pet effects are not automatically modeled.

THJ behavior and stock gear — live testing

The custom AA, spell focus and stock-derived gear update is installed for live testing. Scaling uses 131 researched Legendary items and matching standard EverQuest baselines. Classic level 50 and starter progression are preserved. Reopen the normal launcher for game 2026101902 before testing. See behavior details and open testing limits.

The update makes Improved Damage, Improved Healing, Mana Preservation, Reagent Conservation and Hate Adjustment use their strongest endpoints. Improved Damage is multiplied by 10, with explicit Mage exceptions: Heart of Flame 100% and Fire Core 150%. Damage focuses limited to single-target spells can affect supported area targets while retaining their other restrictions. Bard damage-focus songs keep their random ranges; direct-damage focuses gain 10× while DoT focuses do not. Bard songs receive no spell focus or twincast, and their 3-second base cast becomes 2.5 seconds. These interpretations require playtesting.

Live AA testing: All 16 classes have more earned AA options: 75 newly available lines, 111 expanded lines and Druid access to Healing Boon. No existing line is removed. Classic remains level 50. Reconnect and turn Recommended AA off to browse your held classes. Read the AA update.

Live testing: Direct Spell Damage, ordinary DoT ticks, heroic INT/WIS, pet healing and held-class melee effects have changed. Update through the launcher before testing. Spell-rank choice, mana sustain and burst balance still need player checks.

Cooldown duration repairs

Reuse reductions no longer create extremely long lockouts on item clicks, Mend, Bash, Frenzy and linked spells. Fully reduced cooldowns stay ready instead of restarting old timers on affected skills and AA completion paths. Ordinary reuse and effects that intentionally add time remain. Shared spell and discipline content groups, generic basic attacks, and Begging/Pick Pockets remain under investigation. This live update does not clear existing saved timers.

Blessing effects that survive reconnects

Repairs restore saved buff effects after login and stop permanent blessings expiring on the next tick. You should not need another hail for ordinary blessings. Old nonexpiring XP boosts now receive a minimal countdown on load; positive remaining timers are retained. Player retesting continues.

Raid & Grind dungeons: earlier update details

The Hole entrance

Live testing — keyless Hole entrance: The Hole Key and lock-picking requirement have been removed from the entrance rock in Paineel at /loc 568,-896,-96. Click the rock to open the passage without a key or lock picks. The server update is installed; in-game acceptance is pending. Paineel city-lift keys and the Sacred Key doors inside The Hole remain unchanged.

Live testing — Hate Keeper in Commonlands: Find the Plane of Hate Keeper in East Commonlands at /loc -1570,-346,3, between Mirielle and Khalure in the travel area. Raid, Grind and return entry lead to Hate; private Hate instances retain an entrance Keeper. Public and private Hate entry require level 46; GM status is no longer required. The server update is installed. The owner confirmed the relocation, Commonlands visibility and Hate travel. Broader dungeon balance and full-clear QA remain separate.

Live testing — every Classic dungeon: The installed release extends Raid, Grind, Enter, Join, Status, Claim Rewards and Reset to 21 Classic combat dungeons, including Fear, Hate and Sky. All 21 dungeons and their new rewards are installed for testing. In-game and balance acceptance are pending.

Every Classic dungeon — live testing

Live testing. Added zones: blackburrow, crushbone, runnyeye, soldunga, guktop, gukbottom, mistmoore, kedge, paw, hole, qcat, fearplane, hateplane, airplane. Current native populations are retained; this is not a historical restoration of every zone. Runs keep the existing twelve-hour limit and personal credit requirements.

Added Raid final bosses receive three dungeon-specific exclusive designs in Polished and Ascended versions. All dungeon rewards are MAGIC; existing item IDs and other stats remain unchanged. Managed Sky adds durable key exchangers on each key island, still requiring the normal tokens. Managed Grind gives the four previously scripted Sky bosses eight-hour timers and preserves the princess’s four-hour timer. Public and legacy Sky retain their original behavior. Plane runs isolate their quest state from public zones and other runs.

Keeper placement — live testing: The overlapping Keepers in Befallen, Unrest, Najena, Permafrost and Nagafen’s Lair now have positions 15 units from their waypoints. High Keep and Cazic-Thule already had separate positions and remain unchanged. Visibility is not yet confirmed in game. If an eye is still hidden, use /target Instance_Keeper and hail. Waypoints and dungeon progress are unchanged.

Live testing: Selected dungeon equipment budgets are raised so comparable Normal rewards exceed Ascended starter gear. Modes, objectives, Keepers and eligibility remain unchanged.

Live testing: Raid and Grind dungeon modes are available from all 21 dungeon Keepers. Existing legacy runs keep their original behavior until expiry or reset. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain open.

Raid and Grind choices are available in all 21 Classic combat dungeons listed here, including Fear, Hate and Sky. Each run lasts twelve hours and allows up to six characters. Testing and balance acceptance remain open.

Unique Classic raid rewards — live testing

Live testing: The Classic raid rewards give every dungeon three exclusive designs. The 14 added dungeons contribute 42 designs in two qualities; all 414 dungeon rewards are MAGIC. Fear, Hate and Sky receive lore-driven relics and equipped utility clicks. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

New recommended levels follow each dungeon’s equipment band. Planar items require level 46. All remain permanent, tradeable, non-LORE, zero-resale and outside existing forging recipes. The original seven exclusive families remain, with MAGIC added where needed. Already earned rewards and generated loot keep their identities.

New numeric power stays within the existing band, slot and quality budgets. Their lore is original Nightcap fiction inspired by each dungeon. Each family has Polished and Ascended versions.

Planar relics

Fear: Visage of Unbroken Will reveals the unseen with See Invisible, beside Spine of the Faceless and Dreadhusk of the Last Stand. Its reuse is five minutes.

Hate: Maestro’s Unfinished Requiem grants Invisibility; Innoruuk’s Severed Covenant and Seal of the First Betrayal recall hatred and broken elven royalty. Its reuse is ten minutes.

Sky: Astrolabe of the Eighth Island grants ordinary Levitate, beside Veeshan’s Unwritten Horizon and Mantle of the First Brood. Its reuse is fifteen minutes. Levitate requires one Bat Wing and respects no-levitation zones, including Sky itself; island keys are still required.

Each click requires equipping the item at level 46 and a ten-second cast. Both qualities and duplicate copies share the same family cooldown; Ascended does not improve the utility. Cast/reuse figures are base values subject to native focus reductions. Native targeting, reagent conservation and spell restrictions remain.

Equipment & trading: earlier update details

Find ordinary equipment

Use the loot finder to match your held classes and locate database-dropped equipment within the active era. Each item shows source mobs, zones, spawn locations and calculated drop chances, including ordinary quality upgrades. The Hunt catalog and dungeon guides cover their separate reward systems.

Try the experimental Build Lab to compare stat changes and test spell priorities against explicit combat assumptions. Full gear, AA and pet effects are not automatically modeled.

Live testing: The Classic raid rewards give every dungeon three exclusive designs. The 14 added dungeons contribute 42 designs in two qualities; all 414 dungeon rewards are MAGIC. Fear, Hate and Sky receive lore-driven relics and equipped utility clicks. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

Quest ingredient qualities - live testing

Normal-item quest requirements accept Polished, Exalted and Ascended versions of the same item. Shakrn Meadowgreen in South Karana accepts an Aviak Charm of any ordinary quality plus two Star Rubies for Ascended Crafted Gauntlets, following the current class-armor reward policy. Ingredients are consumed; their quality does not upgrade the configured reward. Exact Normal inputs are used first when both are offered. Explicit quality requirements, reforging recipes and separate epic, hunt and dungeon catalogs retain their own rules. Quest hand-ins and task delivery support the change; in-game acceptance testing remains open.

Classic race robes — live testing

Game update 2026102204 repairs the native model binding behind the waist gap reported on Barbarian and Half Elf. The earlier 2026102203 update did not resolve that gap. The correction covers male and female Half Elves, Wood Elves, Barbarians, Dwarves, Trolls, Ogres and Halflings. Close EverQuest completely, reopen the normal launcher and press Play to update. Other players also need the update to see the corrected models. Equipment eligibility and item stats remain unchanged. Native waist, dye and animation acceptance is still pending.

THJ behavior and stock gear — live testing

The custom AA, spell focus and stock-derived gear update is installed for live testing. Scaling uses 131 researched Legendary items and matching standard EverQuest baselines. Classic level 50 and starter progression are preserved. Reopen the normal launcher for game 2026101902 before testing. See behavior details and open testing limits.

The update uses unmodified stock ProjectEQ as an approximation of standard EverQuest, then preserves the exact researched values where available. It changes 143,332 existing tier definitions across 47,809 eligible ordinary families. Normal items, the 209 starter families, custom Hunt/dungeon rewards, augment families and quest-only epics keep their existing treatment. Families that exceed native stat limits are excluded for review.

Ascended fieldCandidate target from stock

Polished and Exalted receive one-third and two-thirds of the increase from Normal to Ascended. These intermediate formulas and extrapolation beyond the screenshots are Nightcap tuning choices. Attack and sparse utility fields use stock values unless an exact observed override applies. Existing effects, sockets, delays, equip rules, loot routes and owned items are preserved.

Live testing: Selected Ascended items now use reviewed THJ values, including reductions. Starter upgrades remain modest and comparable Normal dungeon gear is stronger. Spell Damage and Healing Amount have 750 base caps, plus earned Hunt headroom.

Manage your pets →

Free trading and no LORE limit

Prepare in the tunnel, then explore

Raid or Grind in all 21 Classic dungeons

Choose your dungeon mode →

A shared home base

Plan your journey →

Lasting blessings; temporary combat abilities

Know which effects last →

Keep fighting while you cast

Damage-over-time spells cast instantly, and melee autoattacks can continue during casting. Mana costs, reuse, resistance and control effects still matter.

Less upkeep between adventures

Healing without changing your target

Custom AA behavior

  • Warlord’s Fury: +100% physical skill damage for up to 12 seconds, 60-second reuse.
  • Gut Punch: initial damage and +50% physical damage taken for up to 12 seconds. Press the Attack lowers AC; Grappling Strike lowers evasion. Their unverified opening/debuff values remain explicit tuning choices.
  • Act of Valor: spends 50% of maximum mana once and heals nearby group members for 2 HP per mana spent.
  • Harvest: activate to restore 40% maximum mana.
  • Mana Burn/Blast/Blaze/Volatile Mana Blaze: spend 10/20/30/40% maximum mana; retain 4 damage per mana as a tuning choice. All reach 15-minute reuse with full Hastened Manaburn. Target immunity rejects the cast without mana or cooldown loss.
  • Silent Casting: all casting classes, one-hour duration, 60-second reuse, suspendable timer. Subtlety and obsolete haste/duration modifiers refund purchased ranks.
  • Dimensional Shielding: separate Wizard AA protecting casting from hits, movement and hostile interrupt effects. Stuns and voluntary cancellation still interrupt. Its 120-second duration and 30-minute reuse are retained-value tuning choices.
  • Pyromancy/Cryomancy: 35% proc chance, initial damage plus DoT, opposite-element resistance reduction and compatibility with other buffs. Existing level/mana/trigger restrictions remain.

Evidence and testing limits

Released THJ notes take precedence over older test notes. “Most” static focuses, endpoint selection, the 10× interpretation and the supported area-target scope require validation. The stock baseline is ProjectEQ, not a recovered THJ or Daybreak database. Five weapon observations support the weapon extrapolation. No level-65 profile, new loot access, automatic AA points or free gear is included. In-game checks must cover mana failures, group healing, refund persistence, song focusing, actual hit damage and gear inspection before gameplay balance is accepted.
